articles.title: Tech stocks power market surge as bond yields and oil prices tumble
articles.summary: Tech stocks surged Monday, with the Nasdaq 100 recording its single best day since early August as a wave of euphoria swept over the markets.
articles.body: Tech stocks surged Monday, with the Nasdaq 100 recording its single best day since early August as a wave of euphoria swept over the markets. The broader Nasdaq Composite index also rose 2.2% to a new all-time closing high. The S&P 500 index soared by 1.5%, also its best day since early last month. The Dow rose more than 360 points, or 0.7%. Chip companies such as ARM Holdings, which spiked 17%, and Intel, which rose 12%, accounted for some of the Nasdaq’s best performing stocks. AMD shares rose nearly 10%, and the company hit a $1 trillion valuation for the first time. Meta Platforms rose a stunning 11.4%, adding nearly $200 billion in market value, fueled by optimism around its AI ambitions and its recently released Muse AI assistant. Monday ranked as Meta’s best one-day stock performance since the global market tariff turmoil of April 2025. The buying was not restricted to tech stocks, however. Shares of Moderna powered higher by 12%. The S&P industrial, real estate and consumer discretionary sectors also posted strong gains. After Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery reached a deal earlier Monday with state attorneys general that likely paves the way for them to close their merger, shares of each company jumped more than 10%. The market moves were largely attributable to a report over the weekend from Fox News Channel’s Trey Yingst, who said he had spoken to President Donald Trump. “The president said he would possibly be open to meeting with Iranian President Pezeshkian” during the United Nations General Assembly in New York this week, Yingst reported Sunday. The reporting raised hopes among investors that the monthslong freeze in any U.S.-Iran talks could end this week, potentially clearing the way for renewed oil traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. Oil prices dropped sharply as a result, with Brent crude oil closing the session Monday at $100.34 per barrel, down 3.4% for the day. U.S. crude oil slid to $95.78, down 4.5% for the session. Also pushing oil prices lower were reports of an increase in Saudi Arabia’s oil flows from Bloomberg News, which cited satellite imagery of oil supertankers filling up. Earlier in the day, Brent dipped below $100 per barrel for the first time since Sept. 9. The S&P’s energy sector was the index’s biggest laggard on Monday, declining 2.5% as the prospect of higher profits evaporated. Monday’s drops marked oil’s fourth straight day of declines, bringing its total decline to 9.5% since Wednesday. Oil prices remain sharply elevated this year, despite its drop in recent days. Since the start of the year, oil has risen more than 65%. As oil prices fell, bond yields followed, fueled by hopes that cheaper oil could lead to lower gas prices, and an overall easing of the inflationary forces rippling through the U.S. economy. In their second straight day of declines, the 10-year Treasury yield fell to 4.96%, after trading as high as 5.02% last week. That specific Treasury bond heavily influences consumer borrowing rates. Still, the average 30-year fixed rate mortgage was still 7.19% on Monday, according to Mortgage News Daily. On Sunday night, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and U.S. Trade Rep. Jamieson Greer hailed “very successful” trade discussions with their counterparts from China. The delegations also discussed AI and potentially lower tariffs on a swath of goods. The prospect of positive developments on the U.S.-China trade front also provided some hope to investors, but not that much. On Monday, Greer shot down speculation about a possible extension of the U.S.-China trade deal that set to expire in November. “Our sense is we aren’t going to have the extension today,” he told Bloomberg News.

articles.title: New Zealand trade pact to take effect on Oct 20, to give duty-free access
articles.summary: India Business News: NEW DELHI: The India-New Zealand free trade agreement (FTA) will come into force on Oct 20 (Dusshera), providing duty-free access to 100% of India’s e.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The India-New Zealand free trade agreement (FTA) will come into force on Oct 20 (Dusshera), providing duty-free access to 100% of India’s exports, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal announced Monday. And, talks with Canada for a comprehensive economic partnership agreement (CEPA) are moving in top gear.“The next 90 days should be a very defining period in the Canada-India relationship. Both sides have resolved to fast-track negotiations, in view of which our team is now slated to go for the fifth round on Oct 5,” Goyal told reporters. The fourth round of negotiations concluded on Sept 18 and the next one is scheduled in just around a fortnight, indicating that two sides are keen to clinch a deal soon. Canada is in the midst of a trade battle with the US and is seen to be keen to expand its trade footprint and reduce its reliance on its neighbour.India’s major exports to Canada include pharmaceuticals, iron and steel, seafood, cotton garments, electronic goods and chemicals. Key imports from Canada include pulses, pearls and semi-precious stones, coal, fertilisers, paper and crude petroleum. Trade between the two countries stood at $30.4 billion in 2025, with an aim to double it to $70 billion by 2030. Besides, Goyal also expressed confidence regarding the trade pact with Chile. “In the coming few months, we will hear some good news,” he said.Regarding the trade agreement with New Zealand, Goyal said it will help boost bilateral trade between the two countries to Rs 35,000 crore and will help facilitate $20 billion investments in India over next 15 years in sectors such as startups, manufacturing and infrastructure.“We are taking forward the next important milestone in our bilateral economic partnership, reflecting our shared commitment to build a stronger and a more ambitious economic partnership,” Goyal said. The two countries had inked the pact in April this year.Currently, New Zealand maintains tariffs of up to 10% on key Indian goods, including ceramics, carpets, automobiles, textiles and auto components. Goyal added that the pact also establishes an agricultural productivity partnership whereby New Zealand’s technology will meet India’s scale and growing demand.For New Zealand, the pact will provide preferential access to the largest and fastest growing economy of the world, he said.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. articles.title: Interests of charitable trust may differ from that of co: JP Morgan chairman & CEO Jamie Dimon
articles.summary: India Business News: MUMBAI: JP Morgan is the world’s most valuable bank, and its chairman and CEO Jamie Dimon is the longest serving chief of a large global bank. In an i.
articles.body: MUMBAI: JP Morgan is the world’s most valuable bank, and its chairman and CEO Jamie Dimon is the longest serving chief of a large global bank. In an interview with TOI, Dimon speaks of what it takes to run America’s largest bank and his definition of success.You completed two decades at JPMorgan this year. What does it take to run a bank successfully for two decades? Is it a conservative approach?I took over Bank One in 2000 which effectively took control of JP Morgan, so it has been closer to 26 years. I consider myself conservative, but banking always involves risk. Good risk-taking is analytical, not guesswork: assess competitors, costs, capital, liquidity and stress scenarios.You need to know the details, study the data and be honest about results. Success is not just profit; it’s about customers, products, execution and how you compare with the best. Have curiosity, courage and grit, and tell the board more about what went wrong than what went right. That is how you improve.When you’re already the most valuable, largest bank, how do you measure success as a CEO?Ultimately, value matters, but a good company is more than profit. Are you retaining, hiring and training good people and building a culture of openness, curiosity and ambition across technology, products and systems? Maximising profit means little if products, systems or compliance fail and regulators are unhappy. You have to judge the whole business.We’re seeing a lot of leadership changes in India. What should the objectives be for a CEO? Should it be just shareholder returns and customer satisfaction, or should it go beyond that?It is about the whole institution: products, services, systems, people, culture, ethics and compliance. In India, that means serving clients while meeting govt and regulatory expectations. If a new system strengthens the business for 20 years, build it even if it hurts near-term profits or the share price. We also measure market share, competition and customer satisfaction because all three matter.You introduced initiatives to help redevelop Detroit. Do you think that large institutions like JPMorgan should go beyond their role in just banking and look at benefiting society? And what’s the best structure for doing good?Absolutely. It is part of our job. In India, we look to help lift the country through how we operate, serve our clients and raise capital. Since 2019, we’ve raised and provided clients with more than $84 billion in capital and credit. And since 2015, we have contributed more than $90 million in donations and helped more than 100,000 young people develop skills and access careers through our partnerships with nonprofits.A healthy company helps clients and lifts society, and philanthropy must also deliver results. In Detroit, we made a multiyear commitment covering jobs, skills and healthcare, bringing all our businesses together. We learned from it and now apply the model in other cities. For CEOs, lifting society means doing both the commercial and philanthropic work.In Detroit, we had a great leader in the mayor who said, “I’ll work with anybody who helps me.” He didn’t say, “I’m not going to speak to business. I’m not going to speak to philanthropy. I’m not going to speak to civil society.” He got everyone to the table to address basic needs such as housing, street lights, ambulances, policing, taxes and schools. He asked for help, acted on it and changed the city.A lot of business houses in Europe and in India, like the Tatas, have a structure where they are owned by charitable trusts, and that’s the route used to do good. Do you think that is the right structure for doing good?I’m not saying it’s always bad. A company should be run properly, and the interests of a charitable trust could be very different from the interests of a company. A company has got to be healthy and vibrant and have proper governance. A structure like that sometimes works against that.I have seen boards in big American companies that are more obsessed with how they look than whether the company is building great products. And that is bad not just for the company, but for society. If the company isn’t healthy and vibrant, if it has the wrong goals, then it’s bad for jobs, capital formation and the country. So you’ve got to be quite careful with something like that.I understand what you are referring to, and, to be clear, I think the world of Chandra. He’s done an extraordinary job in creating value for the foundations. Corporate governance is critical for a successful economy and its companies, and if changes are needed to corporate structures, they should be made.When I walk into the boardroom, I ask the questions: “What’s the right thing to do for the company, its clients and the community?”When do you think the Fed rate hike will start hurting and put stress on businesses?At this point, it doesn’t, but at some point it will start to put stress. I don’t think the short rate is that important; I think it’s more about the 10-year rate. I don’t think one more 25-basis-point rate hike would do it. I’m very sympathetic to those facing stress, but I don’t put that in the systemic category.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Critics say California got too little in deal to let Paramount buy Warner Bros
articles.summary: WASHINGTON, Sept 21 (Reuters) - Critics swiftly decried a California-driven settlement with Paramount Skydance that cleared the way for its $110 billion acqu...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON, Sept 21 (Reuters) - Critics swiftly decried a California-driven settlement with Paramount Skydance that cleared the way for its $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery, saying it will hurt competition in Hollywood, failed to protect jobs and lacks substantial ‌concessions from the media conglomerate.

Opponents of the merger accused California Attorney General Rob Bonta and Governor Gavin Newsom of caving to wealthy interests, particularly ‌Paramount CEO David Ellison, after Paramount threatened to leave the state if the lawsuit was not dropped.

"Today, billionaires have yet again bribed, censored, and bullied their way to the top," said Alvaro Bedoya, ​a former member of the US Federal Trade Commission and adviser at the American Economic Liberties Project. "Layoffs will follow. People from L.A. to Atlanta will lose their jobs, small businesses will lose their contracts, your cable bill and movie ticket will be even more expensive."

Disappointment with the settlement rippled beyond Hollywood, illustrating a growing split in the Democratic Party between moderates, who are more business-friendly, and progressives, who seek a harder line to deliver affordability for US consumers.

US Senator Elizabeth Warren, a Democrat from ‌Massachusetts, criticized the deal, and said Paramount is a "clear candidate ⁠for antitrust scrutiny in a future pro-competition administration."

"This settlement greenlights an anti-monopoly disaster that will result in higher prices and fewer jobs, and enables a handful of billionaires to call the shots in the American media," she said.

Bonta, in a press conference on Monday, said the settlement is "not a vote of support" of the acquisition, because "it does not serve competition well." But he also argued it would amount to more production in California.

Ellison said on Monday that the deal will strengthen competition and benefit consumers and workers.

Spokespeople for Paramount and Bonta did not immediately respond to requests ​for ​comment on the reaction by critics of the deal.

Bonta had said from the outset that ​structural remedies, where a company sells off part of its ‌business, are superior to promises to change or uphold business practices.

Yet the settlement does not require Paramount to sell off any cable channels, or any component of what Bonta said made Paramount and Warner such a formidable combo in theatrical film distribution, such as its lucrative intellectual property.
authors: By Jody Godoy and Chris Sanders

articles.title: GST rate rejig helps consumers upgrade
articles.summary: India Business News: NEW DELHI/MUMBAI: A year after GST rates were cut, automobile dispatches have continued to climb. Several two-wheeler users moved to four-wheelers as .
articles.body: NEW DELHI/MUMBAI: A year after GST rates were cut, automobile dispatches have continued to climb. Several two-wheeler users moved to four-wheelers as price cuts improved affordability, TV buyers have shifted towards larger sets and consumer goods volumes picked up in the Oct-Dec quarter, although they are now under pressure due to the West Asia crisis.Passenger vehicle dispatches reached a record 12.7 lakh units in April–June 2026, up 25.9% from a year earlier, according to Siam. Two-wheeler dispatches rose 20.3% to 56.3 lakh units. Siam has cited lower GST rates and easier financing among the factors supporting demand. Its figures measure supplies to dealers, rather than purchases by customers.Television shipments tell a different story. India’s smart TV shipments grew 10% year-on-year in Oct–Dec 2025, according to Counterpoint Research, before falling 3% in Jan-March 2026. TVs sized 55 inches and above were the fastest-growing category in the March quarter, accounting for nearly one-third of shipments.The trend, however, got stalled because of the uncertainty triggered by Operation Epic Fury US and Israel launched against Iran on Feb 28 and Counterpoint’s TV tracker recorded a 9.8% decline in shipments in April–June. GST on TVs above 32 inches, including 55-inch models, was slashed from 28% to 18% last Sept.Keshav Bansal, director at Intex Technologies, said the cut created “a meaningful affordability window” for bigger TVs. Intex’s consumer durables business grew 80% in FY26, with smart TVs among the drivers, he said. But “unit volumes have not risen in proportion to value growth; the more significant shift has been in product mix,” as buyers chose larger screens and better technology.Bansal said lower GST also supported air-conditioner demand, alongside a favourable summer and a lower comparison base. Rising input costs, including memory chips for TVs, and the cost of meeting newer energy-efficiency norms for ACs have since absorbed part of the tax benefit, he said.“In the long-term, it is definitely a positive, especially with people looking to move to branded products. But there is some impact in the short run due to the recent increase in input prices. Also, full refund of input tax credit will help in offsetting some of the cost,” said Liberty Shoes executive director Anupam Bansal.FMCG companies initially saw an improvement in demand after the rate changes. Volume growth picked up at companies, including Hindustan Unilever, Marico and Dabur. Nestlé India reported its strongest volume growth in five years in the Dec 2025 quarter, attributing it partly to a market recovery supported by GST benefits.That early lift has come under pressure as companies raised prices to offset higher costs. Companies and analysts are keeping a close watch on sales in the current quarter.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Daniel Klabin, herdeiro da empresa de papel e celulose, se torna o bilionário mais velho do Brasil | G1
articles.standfirst: Engenheiro formado em 1952, empresário tem patrimônio ligado à família fundadora da Klabin e acumula mais de sete décadas de atuação nos negócios. Ele assume o posto após a morte de João Jacob Vontobel.
articles.summary: Herdeiro da família fundadora da Klabin, empresário tem fortuna estimada em R$ 1,6 bilhão.
articles.body:
Da esquerda para a direita: presidente da ABF, dr. Edgard Leite, sra. Maria Isabel Klabin e dr. Daniel Miguel Klabin. — Foto: Divulgação/Academia Brasileira de Filosofia

Aos 97 anos, o engenheiro e empresário Daniel Miguel Klabin passa a ocupar o posto de bilionário mais velho do Brasil. Ele assume a posição após a morte de João Jacob Vontobel também aos 97 anos.

Nascido em 11 de maio de 1929, Klabin tem uma fortuna estimada em R$ 1,6 bilhão , segundo o ranking de bilionários da Forbes de 2026.

O patrimônio está baseado em sua participação na estrutura empresarial da família Klabin , fundadora do grupo que se tornou um dos maiores produtores de papel e celulose do país .

Daniel é sócio e diretor-presidente da Daro Participações S.A., holding que participa da estrutura de controle da Klabin. Também dirige a Daram Participações Ltda. e a Daram Comercial Agropecuária Ltda.

Além de herdeiro e acionista da família fundadora, Klabin construiu uma longa trajetória na própria empresa. Ao longo de mais de sete décadas ligado aos negócios familiares, acompanhou diferentes ciclos de expansão da Klabin S.A. e presidiu o Conselho de Administração da companhia em sete ocasiões, nos exercícios de 1981, 1987, 1993, 1999, 2005, 2011 e 2017.

Atualmente, é membro suplente do Conselho de Administração da companhia.

Daniel é filho de Wolff C. Klabin e Rose Haas Klabin e neto de Israel Chaim V. Klabin e Feiga Zlata Lafer. Sua participação nos negócios da família segue uma estrutura em cascata, organizada da seguinte maneira:

Daniel é sócio e diretor-presidente da Daro Participações S.A. e herdeiro da família;

A Daro Participações S.A. é acionista da Klabin Irmãos S.A. (KISA);

E a Klabin Irmãos S.A. é a holding de controle do Grupo Klabin, com 52,3% das ações ordinárias da Klabin S.A. e 19,36% do capital total.

Antes de se tornar uma das figuras mais longevas da família Klabin, Daniel seguiu carreira na engenharia.

Ele se formou em Engenharia Civil em 1952 pela Escola Nacional de Engenharia da Universidade do Brasil, instituição que atualmente corresponde à Escola Politécnica da Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ).

Na juventude, trabalhou em projetos de desenvolvimento industrial no antigo Estado da Guanabara e em outros estados.

Sua trajetória profissional, porém, ficou especialmente ligada aos negócios da família. Na Klabin, participou dos principais ciclos de crescimento da companhia e ocupou posições na governança da empresa durante décadas.

Daniel Klabin é casado com Maria Izabel Catão Klabin. O casal tem três filhos:

Entre os filhos, Amanda ocupa a presidência do Conselho de Administração da Klabin S.A. Ela também é sócia e diretora da Daro Participações S.A. e da Daram Participações Ltda.

Ao longo da trajetória, Daniel recebeu diferentes títulos e condecorações.

Entre eles estão a Medalha Tiradentes e o respectivo diploma, concedidos pela Assembleia Legislativa do Estado do Rio de Janeiro (Alerj) em 2023, e a Cadeira de Membro Titular Notável por Honra ao Mérito da Academia Brasileira de Filosofia, em junho de 2025.

Também recebeu a Ordem do Mérito do Pensamento Brasileiro – Medalha Antonio Paim, em dezembro de 2022, e o título de Doutor Honoris Causa pela Academia Brasileira de Filosofia, em agosto de 2017.

Sua lista de condecorações inclui ainda:

Comendador da Ordem de Rio Branco, em 2002;

Cavaleiro da Ordem do Mérito Militar, em 1999;

Medalha do Pacificador Duque de Caxias, em 1963;

Cidadão Correiapintense, título concedido pela Câmara Municipal de Correia Pinto (SC), em 1992.

articles.title: Vestibular IFPI 2027: Inscrições abertas para 2.740 vagas | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidatos podem solicitar gratuidade da taxa até 28 de setembro; prova será aplicada em 29 de novembro em 23 municípios.
articles.summary: O Vestibular IFPI 2027 oferece 2.740 vagas e candidatos podem solicitar isenção da taxa até 28 de setembro para as provas que ocorrem em novembro.
articles.body:
O Instituto Federal de Educação, Ciência e Tecnologia do Piauí (IFPI) abre, nesta terça-feira (22), as inscrições para o Vestibular 2027 . Ao todo, são ofertadas 2.740 vagas em 78 cursos superiores presenciais, distribuídos em 23 campi no estado.

As inscrições devem ser feitas exclusivamente pela internet, no site selecao.ifpi.edu.br , até 19 de outubro. Para participar, o candidato deve acessar o sistema com uma conta Gov.br. A taxa de inscrição é de R$ 40 e pode ser paga até 20 de outubro, no Banco do Brasil.

Podem solicitar isenção da taxa candidatos inscritos no Cadastro Único para Programas Sociais (CadÚnico) com renda familiar per capita de até meio salário mínimo.

Alunos do 3º ano do ensino médio técnico do IFPI também têm direito à gratuidade.

O pedido deve ser feito no próprio formulário de inscrição, entre os dias 22 e 28 de setembro.

A forma de seleção varia conforme o curso.

Nos cursos de bacharelado e tecnologia, todas as vagas serão preenchidas com base nas notas da prova objetiva e da redação do vestibular.

Já nas licenciaturas, 75% das vagas serão destinadas ao vestibular. Os outros 25% serão preenchidos por meio do Sistema de Seleção Unificada (Sisu), com uso da nota do Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (Enem).

A prova presencial será aplicada em 29 de novembro, das 13h às 18h, nas cidades onde o IFPI possui campi.

O exame será composto por 70 questões objetivas e uma redação em língua portuguesa.

Em literatura, os candidatos deverão estudar as obras "Beira-rio, Beira-vida", de Assis Brasil, e "Crônicas Gonzaguianas", de Wilson Seraine.

O edital prevê reserva de vagas para estudantes de escolas públicas, pessoas pretas, pardas, indígenas, quilombolas e Pessoas com Deficiência (PcD).

Os candidatos que concorrerão às cotas raciais devem solicitar o procedimento de heteroidentificação até 19 de outubro.

No mesmo prazo, os participantes que necessitam de atendimento especial no dia da prova devem enviar a documentação médica pelo site da seleção.

articles.title: CNN, MS NOW and Politico sue Trump, challenging White House ban
articles.summary: WASHINGTON, Sept 21 (Reuters) - CNN, MS NOW and Politico sued President Donald Trump and other members of his administration on Monday for banning them from...
articles.body:
By Susan Heavey, Jonathan Stempel and Helen Coster

WASHINGTON, Sept 21 (Reuters) - CNN, MS NOW and Politico sued President Donald Trump and other members of his administration on Monday for banning them from White House grounds, saying the action violated their rights to free speech and a free press under the US Constitution's First Amendment.

The news outlets are seeking a temporary restraining order to block Trump's action in federal court in Washington, D.C., with a hearing scheduled for Wednesday.

"This ban could not be a ‌more direct assault on the First Amendment nor a more blatant violation of our most fundamental constitutional principles," the lawsuit stated.

"Left unchallenged, this threatens press freedom and the public's right to independent journalism free from government interference," the outlets wrote in a joint statement. "The ‌government does not decide what the press reports or publishes."

Trump announced the ban on Friday on social media, saying those news outlets "shouldn't be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they're covering the President of the United States," and defended it in another post on Monday.

"The White House is not instituting an assault on the Free Press, ​something which I cherish. It is instituting an assault on the FAKE NEWS. It is a threat to our National Security, and must be stopped, NOW!" Trump wrote on Monday, without providing evidence of a national security threat.

Past presidents have battled with the press, but Trump's campaign against the media has been unprecedented. He has upended decades of tradition by denying basic access to many major news organizations, launching personal attacks on journalists for their reporting and elevating media outlets seen as more sympathetic to the administration. He also has filed lawsuits against multiple news outlets.

The White House launched a "Trump TV" stream on Monday evening, days after Trump banned the media outlets from the White House.

The White House said the stream will run videos and highlights of what it calls the Trump administration's achievements but a press freedom advocate said it amounted to "a steady diet of government propaganda."

A 60-second trailer displayed the Republican leader's 2024 presidential ‌win and the first video streamed after the platform went live was Trump's remarks on July ⁠3 at Mount Rushmore. The stream had only about 8,000 live views 15 minutes after it was launched on YouTube.

"This just makes it even clearer that the real goal here is to ensure that the American public is fed a steady diet of government propaganda," Jameel Jaffer, executive director of the Knight First Amendment Institute at Columbia University, said.
authors: By Susan Heavey, Jonathan Stempel and Helen Coster

articles.title: Gold Edges Higher as Lower Oil Prices Damp Chance of Rate Hikes
articles.summary: Gold edged higher as a slump in oil prices over the past few sessions reduced the chance of further interest-rate hikes by the Federal Reserve to contain inf...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Gold edged higher as a slump in oil prices over the past few sessions reduced the chance of further interest-rate hikes by the Federal Reserve to contain inflation.

Bullion was trading around $4,360 an ounce, reversing course after falling the most in a week the day before. Oil steadied on Tuesday after losing more than 9% over the previous four days on easing concern around Middle East exports and a renewed bout of diplomacy to end the US-Iran war.

President Donald Trump is set to address the United Nations General Assembly in New York later Tuesday and has indicated that he's open to meeting his Iranian counterpart, Masoud Pezeshkian, on the sidelines of the gathering. The decline in oil prices has reduced inflationary concerns, a tailwind for gold that typically benefits when rates are lower.

Traders are also tracking comments by Fed officials for clues on the path for rates after the unanimous vote last week to hike for the first time in three years. Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said Monday the US central bank cannot ignore repeated and persistent supply shocks, and must respond in a way that may cause economic hardship. St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said additional rate rises may be needed to achieve the central bank's inflation goal, which hasn't been met in more than five years.

Gold is "holding extremely strong" following the rate-hike with hawkish outlook, with falling energy prices offering support, Ryan McKay, an analyst at TD Securities, wrote in a note. "Despite a hiking cycle being priced in, the broader precious metals landscape remains extremely favorable," with near-term weakness "increasingly seen as a buying opportunity," he dded.

Confidence in the long-term outlook for the metal has also prompted some dip-buying in recent weeks. There have been around 50 tons of inflows into bullion-backed exchange-traded funds so far in September, a third month of gain.

Investors are also eyeing this week's summit between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, with officials offering upbeat assessments ahead of talks expected to cover artificial intelligence, trade and investment. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent described weekend meetings with China's top trade negotiator Li Chenggang as "very successful."

articles.title: Small-city ecomm surges, but order values trail big mkts
articles.summary: India Business News: Ecommerce orders surge beyond India’s top 96 cities (57% of 200m), but deliver just 39% of value; AOV Rs 830 vs Rs 1,714 in big cities.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Online shopping is expanding beyond India’s biggest cities, but the value of those purchases remains concentrated in larger markets.Of more than 200 million orders processed in the last 12 months up to July this year, 57.2% originated outside the 96 largest cities, but these orders accounted for only 39.3% of total transaction value. Their average order value was Rs 830, less than half the Rs 1,714 recorded in the largest cities.EasyEcom, an ecommerce software company, compiled the data from transactions processed through marketplaces, brand websites, quick-commerce platforms, distributors and other channels connected to its system. Its customers include Borosil, Cred, Minimalist and Pilgrim, among others.The gap suggests that ecommerce growth outside the biggest cities is driven more by higher transaction volumes than by higher-value purchases. This could have implications for brands deciding where to hold inventory and how to manage deliveries across a wider network.The divide is even sharper at the state level. Of the 15 largest states in the dataset, 13 changed position when ranked by transaction value rather than order volume.Haryana moved from 11th by orders to third by value, supported by higher-value transactions in Gurugram and Sonipat. Its average order value of Rs 3,804 was more than six times Bihar’s Rs 609. Bihar moved in the opposite direction, falling from 10th by volume to 15th by value.At the city level, Bengaluru was the largest market by order count, with around 11 million orders, 84% more than Mumbai. Gurugram ranked only seventh by volume but second by value, at Rs 1,848 crore. Its average order value of Rs 6,693 was more than four times Delhi’s Rs 1,499.“India’s commerce map has expanded much faster than its economics have converged,” said EasyEcom co-founder and CEO Punit Gupta.EasyEcom processed 112.3 million orders between February and July 2026, up 19.3% from 94.1 million in the preceding six months.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. articles.title: 'No burden for consumers': Sitharaman clarifies who will pay MDR on UPI transactions
articles.summary: India Business News: Union finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman has backed the recently announced Merchant Discount Rate (MDR), saying that the mechanism will be imposed on.
articles.body: Union finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman has backed the recently announced Merchant Discount Rate (MDR), saying that the mechanism will be imposed on operators and will not be passed on to customers. Addressing ongoing speculations around the charges, FM blamed the opposition for creating confusion and urged people to remain alert.Speaking to ANI, the finance minister said that she had already addressed the issue in Parliament, stressing that MDR is a charge between payment operators and will not be 'burdened' on UPI users.Sitharaman stressed that MDR is neither a tax nor a cess and that the money collected through it will not go into the Consolidated Fund of India.”It does not apply to transactions below Rs 2,000. It is neither a tax nor a cess; the funds will not be deposited into the Consolidated Fund of India. It is a charge levied by service providers to improve the system and provide better service, not for small transactions. Moreover, it is a charge between operators; it will not be passed on to the consumer. The burden does not fall on the customer,” she said.Sitharaman said she had given the same clarification earlier too, when the issue came up during the parliamentary session.“I provided a clarification on this very point when the issue was raised during the parliamentary session. Spreading misinformation, fueling debates based on it, and using that narrative to attack the government has become a habit for the opposition. This is wrong; there is an effort to spread misconceptions and mislead the public. The public needs to remain vigilant," Sitharaman added.Meanwhile, Niti Aayog NITI Aayog vice chairman Ashok Kumar Lahiri had also backed the Centre’s decision to introduce a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on high-value UPI transactions, saying that businesses should find ways to sustain themselves instead of relying on government subsidies.Lahiri drew on the words of ancient philosopher Chanakya to make his point, saying a ruler should collect taxes from citizens as a bee collects honey from a flower — “gently, gradually, and without inflicting pain or bruising the petals”.“So you have to find ways of sustaining businesses without having to give subsidy,” Lahiri told reporters on the sidelines of an event.He clarified that the view was his personal opinion and did not represent NITI Aayog’s official position.The government has ruled out any rethink on the decision, with a senior official telling PTI, “There is no question of a re-think.”FM Sitharaman’s clarification comes after the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) introduced a new MDR framework on September 15. Under the framework, an MDR of 0.4 per cent will apply to Person-to-Merchant (P2M) UPI transactions above Rs 2,000, subject to a cap of Rs 300 per transaction.Consumers will continue to transact free of cost using UPI. The government has said that around 96 per cent of P2M transactions will remain unaffected, while the MDR will be distributed among payment ecosystem participants, including banks and payment application providers.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. articles.title: Asian benchmarks mostly rise after Wall Street's rally
articles.summary: Asian shares mostly rose early Tuesday, as the market mood turned positive from the overnight rally on Wall Street.  Hong Kong's Hang Seng gained nearly 0.6%...
articles.body:
TOKYO (AP) — Asian shares mostly rose early Tuesday, as the market mood turned positive from the overnight rally on Wall Street.

Australia's S&P/ASX 200 added 02% in early trading to 8,748.20. South Korea's Kospi jumped 1.6% to 7,120.25. Hong Kong's Hang Seng gained nearly 0.6% to 25,185.26, while the Shanghai Composite rose 0.4% to 3,964.45. Tokyo markets were closed for an extended holiday and trading resumes Thursday.

Wall Street climbed to the edge of its all-time high Monday. The S&P 500 jumped 1.5% and pulled within 0.4% of its record set last month. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 366 points, or 0.7%, and the Nasdaq composite leaped 2.3% to its own all-time high as chip stocks and other companies in the artificial-intelligence industry led the way.

Stocks have been getting help from the recent decline in oil prices, although they rose in Asian trading. In energy trading, benchmark U.S. crude gained 0.43% to $96.19 a barrel. Brent, the international standard, rose 0.65% to $100.99 a barrel.

That's still much higher than its roughly $72 price from earlier this summer, but it's down from the nearly $110 it touched last week.

Oil prices have been swinging as some crude passed through the Strait of Hormuz to get to customers, though nowhere near as much as the industry would like because of conflicts in the Middle East.

Monday's pullback in oil prices helped lower the pressure coming from the bond market. The yield on the 10-year Treasury eased to 4.95% from 5.01% late Friday after crossing above the 5% threshold last week for the first time since 2023.

Global markets are also getting a boost recently from AI stocks, which are continuing to strengthen following their worldwide slide at the start of last week. Leaders of the industry have recently warned a slowdown is needed in the industry's development for the safety of humanity.

All told, on Wall Street, the S&P 500 rose 114.20 points to 7,764.70. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 366.19 to 52,048.83, and the Nasdaq composite climbed 599.55 to 27,122.09.

In currency trading, the U.S. dollar edged up to 157.43 Japanese yen from 157.31 yen. The euro cost $1.1474. up from $1.1469.

AP Business Writer Stan Choe contributed to this report.

articles.title: 20 countries propose global oversight body to manage AI dangers
articles.summary: Countries including Germany, South Africa and Canada suggest international institution to set and enforce standards.
articles.body:
Twenty countries and the European Union have issued a call for international cooperation to ensure AI remains under human control, including the potential creation of a global oversight body to set and enforce standards.

The countries, including Germany, South Africa, Canada, Australia, the United Arab Emirates and Singapore, issued the joint statement on Monday as global leaders prepare to discuss the risks posed by rapidly advancing AI at the annual gathering of the United Nations General Assembly.

The declaration, released by the office of Finnish President Alexander Stubb, calls on governments and industry to act immediately to ensure that AI is developed in line with international law and remains under “human direction, oversight and control”.

“To realise AI’s potential, industry, governments and society must act now,” the statement says.

“We must address these risks and strengthen oversight – without widening the gap between countries in access to the benefits of AI.”

The declaration urges countries to develop and coordinate “common standards”, share reports of serious safety incidents, and explore the establishment of an international institution to “set standards, enable verification, and convene states when capability thresholds are crossed”.

Signatories include German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, Kenyan President William Ruto, Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan.

The United States and China, the world’s two leading AI powers, did not join the statement, which remains “open for endorsement” by other countries.

US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are expected to discuss AI when they meet at the White House on Thursday for their third face-to-face summit in less than a year.

Washington and Beijing, which are in a race to dominate cutting-edge technologies, have both rebuffed calls to slow down AI development to ensure greater safety.

Other AI players not among the signatories include India, South Korea, Japan, the UK and France.

The declaration comes as the AI sector is engaged in a heated debate about safety following calls for a slowdown in development by top industry leaders.

In an essay earlier this month, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called on firms to “slow the pace” of development to mitigate risks, a proposal that was swiftly endorsed by rivals including OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk.

Amodei’s call followed a series of cases of AI models engaging in unsanctioned malign activity, including an incident in July in which AI agents being tested by OpenAI hacked the AI start-up Hugging Face.

In the latest intervention by industry on Monday, OpenAI said the US should lead an international effort to develop technical standards for advanced AI.

“The United States is well positioned to lead because its AI industry is at the technical frontier, and it still stands in a privileged global network position in critical areas such as finance, trade, defense, technology, and information systems,” the San Francisco-based AI giant said in a blog post.

“Leading now will determine whether the United States shapes the global AI framework or watches a fragmented, uneven, and conflict-ridden system take hold around it.”

The UN-backed Independent International Scientific Panel on AI, which examined the Hugging Face incident, on Monday also added its voice to calls for new guardrails, saying the cyberattack had exposed the “unravelling” of existing safeguards.

articles.title: Why Japan’s markets matter so much for America
articles.summary: From surging bond yields to US intervention to support the yen, Japan’s financial markets are undergoing major shifts that have consequences for investors and borrowing costs around the globe.
articles.body: From surging bond yields to US intervention to support the yen, Japan’s financial markets are undergoing major shifts that have consequences for investors and borrowing costs around the globe. Bond yields in Japan have soared to their highest levels in three decades, boosted by inflation, the Bank of Japan raising interest rates and investors’ concerns about the government’s spending plans. Meanwhile, the yen continues to fluctuate after a historic joint intervention by Washington and Tokyo. The moves in Japan’s bonds and currency have reverberations across the global economy. Japan is the largest foreign holder of US Treasuries, making it a key player for how much money flows in or out of US bond markets. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has embarked on an extraordinary campaign this year to intervene in markets to support the yen. Analysts say Bessent’s actions aim to prevent Japan from selling its dollar assets – like Treasuries – to boost the value of the yen. Further selling in Treasuries could push up US interest rates when there are concerns about affordability and a steady rise in yields. The US and Japanese financial markets are becoming increasingly intertwined. And their relationship is back in focus this week as world leaders gather in New York City for the UN General Assembly. President Donald Trump and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi are expected to meet Tuesday. Here’s what to know about recent changes in Japan’s markets, and why there are ripple effects across US and global markets. Bond market Stubborn inflation, higher central bank interest rates and nerves about government spending have driven borrowing costs higher across the globe. Japan has been among the hardest hit in the bond market sell-off. Yields on 10-year government bonds in the United States, France, Germany and the United Kingdom have climbed to their highest levels in nearly 20 years. In Japan, the 10-year yield recently hit its highest level in 30 years. The rise in yields is a sign that economies across the world are entering an era of higher interest rates — and exiting the era of ultra-low interest rates that became a defining feature of the global economy after the 2008 financial crisis. The Bank of Japan — or BOJ — started raising interest rates in 2024, a major change after decades of ultra-low rates aimed at combating deflation. The BOJ hiked rates just last week in an effort to cool down inflation, its second increase this year. Bond yields rise when prices fall. Bond prices have slumped in Japan, sending yields soaring, as investors adjust to persistent inflation and the BOJ raising rates. Meanwhile, markets are trying to assess Takaichi’s budget plans. Investors are wary of her plans for tax cuts and increased government spending, which would swell borrowing needs when Japan already has an enormous debt load. In turn, they’re demanding more compensation – or higher yields – to hold Japan’s debt. The rise in Japan’s yields matters for global markets because it can push up yields elsewhere, including the United States. It also shows how concerns about government spending can translate into higher borrowing costs as investors demand more compensation. Meanwhile, higher yields in Japan can make buying Japan bonds more attractive for investors – who could pull money out of other markets. The yen Currency markets are also in focus ahead of the expected Trump-Takaichi meeting Tuesday. The US Treasury in late July intervened in currency markets to boost the yen after the Japanese currency hit its lowest level against the dollar in 40 years. The move was a historic joint intervention with Japan. The yen hasn’t re-touched those lows since then, but it has weakened closer to those lows in recent weeks. Analysts say the intervention was aimed in part at preventing Japan from selling assets, including US Treasuries, to support its own currency. Data released by the Treasury Department showed Japan reduced its holding of Treasuries in May, June and July. If Japan sells Treasuries, it can push prices lower and yields higher. That’s put more attention on the trajectory of the yen. Bessent has notably taken interest in trying to manage how Japan’s currency markets impact US markets. “There are a multitude of factors that at a minimum could create quite a bit of volatility in the market and weigh on the US Treasury market,” Adam Turnquist, chief technical strategist at LPL Financial, said. “I think that’s why you’re seeing more and more conversation and commentary from the Treasury about how the Bank of Japan should handle their monetary policy.” Traders are also on alert for just how strong the yen becomes. A strengthening yen while the BOJ is raising interest rates could unravel the so-called carry trade, where investors borrow cheap yen to invest in higher-yielding assets. If the yen rapidly strengthens while Japan’s interest rates are already rising, it suddenly becomes more costly to borrow in yen and investors could be forced to sell their other assets – like stocks and US Treasuries – to close their trade. While the United States wants to avoid the yen weakening so much that Japan has to sell assets to boost its currency, it also doesn’t want the yen to strengthen so fast that it draws investors away from other markets like the US. It’s a fine line to walk and highlights the sensitivity of US markets to what happens in Japan. Any sharp moves in Japan’s bond and currency markets could ripple through to global markets and affect US investors. “Stability is key,” Turnquist said.
